title: Premarket · Tuesday 9/22

headline.title: This book called META wrong yesterday, and the reason is worth more than the trade. It read Friday's Outside (3) closing near its low at a six-month high and said no long. META closed Monday at $741.24, +11.34%. The structure was real and it did not matter — Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, had become the most-downloaded free iPhone app in the US three days running, and a product launch is not in a candle.
headline.summary: That move carried the tape. AMD +9.95% and through $1 trillion for the first time, on the argument that agentic AI runs on CPUs, not only GPUs. QQQ +2.78%, SPY +1.55%. And it is not finished: Meta Connect is tomorrow and Thursday, 9/23–9/24. This morning SHOP +4% on a deal putting Shop Pay inside Muse — and Amazon has blocked Muse from its own store, which tells you what they think it is. The lesson is not that structure failed. It is that this book used a candle to overrule a catalyst it had not checked for — the second time in three sessions, after reading STX's mid-side print as bearish into a +6.93% session.

overview:
Crude is in freefall and the reason is dated. WTI −2.6% to $93.30, Brent −1.9% to $98.39 — that is $97.59 yesterday morning and $100.70 Thursday. Reuters reports Iran is ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US lifts its port blockade. Bessent says all Iranian airlines lose service Wednesday. Pressure and diplomacy at once, and the tape is paying for the diplomacy.

The energy call worked. This book said below 161.31 the commodity won the argument. XOM broke it, closed 158.30, −3.20%, and is 156.38 now. Jefferies cut MPC and VLO to Hold — the refiners were the bearish-kicker view yesterday and are −2.4% and −2.3% again.

The GLP-1 trade has a new leg. VKTX +23.5% on VK2735 maintenance data — 22% placebo-adjusted weight loss with support for less-frequent dosing. NVO closed −7.96% Monday after its capital markets day, well past the −4.30% it showed premarket. LLY −1.20%.

A regulatory hit, not a sentiment one. DGX −6.5% and LH −5.8%: CMS will cut Medicare lab reimbursement by the statutory maximum 15% from 2027, saving ~$1B a year, after finding Medicare pays 16% more than private payors. That framework has been frozen since 2014.

Earnings: VICR +9.4% — Q3 sequential revenue growth now >20%, double the prior ~10%, on royalties from the Vertical Power Delivery license this book flagged at +12% on 9/17. ONON +11.6% on Investor Day targets. AZO +1.7%, THO +1.8%.

Today: Richmond Fed 9:00 · $78B 2-year auction 12:00 · Williams, Jefferson and Barkin all speak. KBH after the close.

Premarket 30.50 against a 27.32 close. Monday's high was 27.60 — the gap clears the entire prior range, so the level is Monday's high, far below. Let the opening range set the line rather than guessing at one.

Targets plus a buyback plus a reiterated current year is the combination that holds an investor-day gap. The sell-the-news pattern usually needs a vague number or a cut guide, and there is neither here.
Our own investor-day study ran 4 of 5 sell-the-news, and 3 of 5 gapped up and closed below the open. Volume in the first thirty minutes is what separates them — that was INTU's tell.
So watch the 9:00 candle, not the gap. A +11.6% investor-day gap on affirmed guidance is exactly the setup that study says to verify before trusting.

VK2735 maintenance data: 22% placebo-adjusted weight loss, and support for less-frequent dosing regimens. The dosing detail is the competitive point — that is where share moves.
★ No level to trade against. Monday's high 30.28 is far below spot. Let the first 30 minutes build a range, then use it. A 23% gap on trial data has no structure until the session makes one.
The sector read is doing the confirming: NVO closed −7.96% Monday off its own capital markets day, and LLY is −1.20% this morning.
NVO's CEO flagged loss of US semaglutide exclusivity in 2032 as the key challenge. A credible less-frequent-dosing competitor is precisely the threat that framing invites.
Binary biotech on a gap is the worst risk-reward on the board. On the page because the sector read matters, not because it is a $50 trade.

r
CMS cutting Medicare lab reimbursement by the statutory maximum 15% from 2027 — roughly $1B annually — after finding Medicare pays 16% more than private payors. LH −5.8% with it.
The spread is 225.25 bid against 233.95 ask. That is an indicative print, not a tradeable one. Do not touch it until the spread closes after the open.
A rule change reprices once and stays repriced. That is different from a downgrade, which is an opinion the tape can vote against — as ACN did the very next morning.
The framework has been frozen since 2014, so this is a one-time convergence to private-sector rates rather than an ongoing squeeze. The cut lands in 2027.
Two names, one rule, same direction. If it fades hard into the open, that is the market pricing a 2027 event in 2026 — which is usually too early.

g

Monday's high 226.40 is well below spot at 245. No usable level until the open prints one. Watch whether it holds the gap, which is the whole question on a guidance raise.
This book had VICR at +12% on 9/17 on the news it had “granted a leading AI OEM a non-exclusive license” for those modules. This is that license turning into a number, five sessions later.
That is the cleanest kind of follow-through — a licensing announcement is a promise, a guidance raise is the cash. Patent monetization on AI power infrastructure.
Worth keeping as a template: when a license gets announced, the guidance raise is the trade, and it arrives weeks later on a scheduled report.

“Want the pullback that holds 196.21, not the gap.” The pullback never came — Monday's low was 200.65 — so there was no entry. And the gap-buyer lost: 204.31 premarket to a 201.05 close.

This is the version of discipline that looks wrong and is not. Refusing an extended entry and then watching it close red is the system working, even though it shows as a missed green day.
Bitcoin's run has cooled and COIN is red premarket for the first time in four sessions, after +11.66% and +3.50%.
The SEC innovation exemption is still the catalyst and has not changed. A structural rule change does not expire in three sessions — but the entry price does.

darkpool.note: No fresh single-name tape for this session yet. What stands from Friday's expiration board is the record itself: SPCX $9.4B at the ask, the largest single-name print this board has shown, roughly eight times NVDA's $1.2B and on a company public only since its May IPO — and $18.7B cumulative (ask), ahead of NVDA $8.7B (ask) and AAPL $7.6B (ask), all three top names on the same side. Ten single names printed $1B or more against a Thursday board that topped out at $848M. The split held a clean line: memory and power on the bid (QCOM $1.7B, BE $1.3B, SKHY $1.1B), mega-caps and oil majors on the ask (AAPL, NVDA, XOM $1.2B, CVX $1.1B) — and the energy ask prints have now been vindicated twice over, with WTI down 7.4% in three sessions and XOM through the 161.31 line. That is the one lean on the Friday board that price has confirmed. Treat the rest loosely: quad-witching moves size for mechanical reasons, and this book has two live reminders of what over-reading a side costs — STX's mid print called bearish into +6.93%, and META's candle called over its catalyst into +11.34%.
darkpool.right_note: Yesterday's morning tape had META $28M at the bid leading the board on its dividend day, and the board put META on the bullish-kicker view while this book argued the candle said otherwise. The board was right and it was not close. Also still open: ECHO $150P 12/18/26 at $8.6M, a floor put to December, and PANW $360C 09/25, which expires Friday.
